title: New planet, who dis?
description:
Hidden away deep in the Milky Way, a potential new planet has been spotted. Catchily named - right now - ED138, experts reckon it could measure up to 1,500 kilometres wide and sits beyond Pluto, in a part of the sky that is crowded with millions of stars. But, an incredibly powerful telescope in Chile that monitors the sky managed to spot it.

Experts say it could be the discovery of a generation! But ED138 needs to undergo a few checks before it can be officially declared a dwarf planet. So, what are those tests? And what else are we missing? Astronomer Dr Jenifer Millard breaks it all down for us.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討天文學家在冥王星軌道之外發現潛在矮行星的重大突破。天體物理學家 Jennifer Millard 博士說明了定義行星與矮行星的標準，並介紹位於智利的 Vera Rubin 天文台如何運用超大數位相機與演算程式，在每日產生的 10 TB 資料中捕捉到該天體，同時解釋其因距離遙遠且藏身於銀河系密集星群中而長期未被發現的原因。
summaryEn: Astronomers using the Vera Rubin Observatory in Chile may have discovered a new dwarf planet beyond Pluto's orbit. Astrophysicist Dr. Jennifer Millard explains the criteria defining dwarf planets, how complex software processes 10 terabytes of daily data from the telescope to spot mysterious space objects, and why this faint, slow-moving body remained hidden within the crowded stars of the Milky Way for so long.
